endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: AI training restriction: If the vendor is not permitted to train or fine-tune models on your data, this must be stated explicitly.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Reserve the right to audit third-party vendors for compliance with the data use agreement and impose penalties for non-compliance.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether tiered enforcement, cure periods, or suspension and termination clauses in AI vendor contracts lead to vendor remediation or a safe exit, and no study documents the hazard itself. The recommendation rests on two endorsements, and only one of them addresses enforcement directly.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The two endorsements are expert guidance, and guidance does not substitute for comparative data on outcomes such as time to remediation or contract exit.

The RUAIH guidance tells organizations to reserve audit rights and impose penalties for noncompliance with data use agreements, which partly supports tiered enforcement. The CHAI playbook statement requires an explicit clause on model training restrictions. It concerns contract content rather than enforcement triggers, timelines, or termination rights, so it supports R407 only indirectly.

commentary.research_gap: No study measures whether specific enforcement clauses, such as defined performance triggers, cure timelines, or suspension rights, change vendor behavior after an AI failure or breach. Useful designs would compare remediation time, frequency of exercised termination, and patient-facing disruption across health systems with and without such clauses, or would analyze a series of actual contract disputes involving AI vendors.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may hold less negotiating power with vendors, and whether they can obtain and use these contract terms remains unknown.
